Thought: Strong acids are substances that completely dissociate in water, releasing a high concentration of hydrogen ions (H+). The pH scale ranges from 0 to 14, with lower values indicating higher acidity. Strong acids typically have very low pH values because they release many H+ ions in solution. Strong non-oxidizing acids like hydrochloric acid (HCl), hydrobromic acid (HBr), hydroiodic acid (HI), sulfuric acid (H2SO4), and perchloric acid (HClO4) generally have pH values less than 2 in their concentrated forms. In fact, many concentrated strong acids have pH values close to 0 or even negative in extreme cases.
Final Answer: Strong non-oxidizing acids have a very low pH due to their complete dissociation in water and high concentration of hydrogen ions. Their pH values are typically less than 2.
